Q: GitHub-flavored Markdown and Pygments highlighting in Jekyll A:

Easier in later versions

As of Jekyll 0.12.1, redcarpet2 is natively supported by Jekyll, so you can simply set your configuration to markdown: redcarpet and you are good to go with GFM / fenced code blocks without the rest of this mumbo jumbo...

For older versions

You explicitly ask for GitHub-flavored Markdown content, so I presume you aren't looking for answers that create code blocks with the non-Markdown liquid format:

{% highlight python %}
def yourfunction():
     print "Hello, World!"
{% endhighlight %}

but would rather be able to write something with fenced code blocks:

def yourfunction():
     print "Hello, World!"

etc. For this, you will want to use the redcarpet Markdown_ parser.

GitHub-flavored markdown uses a Markdown parser called Redcarpet. Ironically, though GitHub-flavored Markdown uses redcarpet2, this Markdown parser is not supported by Jekyll by default. Instead, you can add this as a plugin by installing that Ruby gem:

gem install redcarpet

And then adding the redcarpet2 Jekyll plugin. (Installing a plugin in Jekyll amounts to placing the .rb ruby script given in that repository into your _plugins directory. It can be in a subdirectory of _plugins too).

Then, as explained on the documentation there, edit your _config.yml file to use redcarpet2:

markdown: redcarpet2
redcarpet:
  extensions: ["no_intra_emphasis", "fenced_code_blocks", "autolink", "strikethrough", "superscript"]

which adds the common extensions provided by GitHub-flavored-Markdown AKA redcarpet2 (Well, almost. This won't do GitHub-specific Markdown things, like identify issues by number, or commits by hash, so they aren't technically the same).

Having the plugin means, for the moment, you will have to build your site locally and copy the _site to github if you are hosting your site there, as redcarpet2 isn't available on the GitHub version of the Jekyll engine (see this open issue on Jekyll).

Note: You don't need all the markdown editors you've specified in your _config.yml by the way. For a basic example using redcarpet2, you might want to see this config and the associated Jekyll directory that goes with it.

Q: How to join tow times the same table? A:

You should not use from('match, team') It creates a wrong cross join. Just use match and join team twice with aliases.

$this->db->select('match.*, team_a.name as home_team, team_b.name as away_team')
         ->from('match')
         ->join('team AS team_a', 'match.team_home_id = team_a.team_id')
         ->join('team AS team_b', 'match.team_away_id = team_b.team_id')
         ->get()
         ->result();

Q: How to use mod_rewrite or url remapping for assets folder in CodeIgniter A:

Add the .htaccess to the root of the codeigniter installation with the following code, or any other similar code, that allows the removal of index.php from the URL and remove the index.php from the config file.

RewriteEngine on
RewriteCond $1 !^(index\.php|system|assets)
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ index.php?/$1 [L]

Now, the .htaccess in the assets sub-folders should work.

Q: Delete multiple rows based off of cell value in VBA A:

Code fixed - solution 1 - Define the Exact Count

Sub DeleteBundleDependents_ByNames()

    Dim ws As Worksheet, deleteRng As Range, bundles As Object
    Dim i As Long, j As Long, lastRow As Long
    Dim dependentList As String

    Set ws = ActiveSheet
    lastRow = ws.Cells(ws.Rows.Count, "A").End(xlUp).Row

    Set bundles = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
    bundles.CompareMode = vbTextCompare
    
    ' Instead of "True", define the EXACT NAMES of the dependents to delete.
    ' IMPORTANT: Commas at the beginning and end are required for an exact match search.
    bundles("Spaghetti") = ",Pasta,Sauce,"
    bundles("Omelette") = ",Eggs,Cheese,Ham,"

    For i = 2 To lastRow
        If bundles.Exists(ws.Cells(i, 1).Value) Then
            dependentList = bundles(ws.Cells(i, 1).Value)
            j = i + 1
            
            ' Loop down as long as it finds 0-cost items
            Do While j <= lastRow And ws.Cells(j, 2).Value = 0
                ' DELETE ONLY IF the item name is present in the bundle's dependent list
                If InStr(1, dependentList, "," & ws.Cells(j, 1).Value & ",", vbTextCompare) > 0 Then
                    If deleteRng Is Nothing Then 
                        Set deleteRng = ws.Rows(j) 
                    Else 
                        Set deleteRng = Union(deleteRng, ws.Rows(j))
                    End If
                End If
                j = j + 1
            Loop
        End If
    Next i

    If Not deleteRng Is Nothing Then deleteRng.Delete Shift:=xlUp

End Sub

Solution 2 Define the Exact Count

Sub DeleteBundleDependents_ByCount()

    Dim ws As Worksheet, deleteRng As Range, bundles As Object
    Dim i As Long, j As Long, lastRow As Long
    Dim dependentCount As Long

    Set ws = ActiveSheet
    lastRow = ws.Cells(ws.Rows.Count, "A").End(xlUp).Row

    Set bundles = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
    bundles.CompareMode = vbTextCompare
    
    ' Tell the code EXACTLY HOW MANY items make up the bundle
    bundles("Spaghetti") = 2
    bundles("Omelette") = 3

    For i = 2 To lastRow
        If bundles.Exists(ws.Cells(i, 1).Value) Then
            dependentCount = bundles(ws.Cells(i, 1).Value)
            
            ' Loop ONLY for the specified number of rows/dependents
            For j = 1 To dependentCount
                ' Check to avoid going out of bounds and ensure the cost is actually 0
                If (i + j) <= lastRow Then
                    If ws.Cells(i + j, 2).Value = 0 Then
                        If deleteRng Is Nothing Then 
                            Set deleteRng = ws.Rows(i + j) 
                        Else 
                            Set deleteRng = Union(deleteRng, ws.Rows(i + j))
                        End If
                    End If
                End If
            Next j
            
        End If
    Next i

    If Not deleteRng Is Nothing Then deleteRng.Delete Shift:=xlUp

End Sub

Both of these approaches will protect your standalone zero-cost items from being accidentally deleted."
